name: Viral SEO
tagline: An AI tool that spits out SEO-targeted articles and programmatic landing pages to chase search traffic.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The generation half of this is a thin wrapper: a prompt, a template, a loop over keywords, markdown out. What you cannot conjure in a session is the data layer, keyword volumes, difficulty scores, live SERP results and competitor page structure, all of which come from paid APIs that these tools quietly resell. So a one-shot build gets you a working article factory that is guessing about demand, which is the part that decides whether any of it ranks. Publishing is the other tax: pushing to WordPress or Webflow or a headless CMS on a schedule is fiddly OAuth work, not fun work. Buildable over a weekend if you accept a bring-your-own-keyword-list workflow and paste your own SERP research in.
coreLoopDIY: Takes a list of keywords plus a site brief, generates internally linked SEO articles and programmatic pages as markdown with proper metadata, and writes them into a static site repo.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env
Your own keyword list, or a paid keyword data API key if you want volumes
A static site or CMS you control to publish into
whatYouLose: Keyword volume and difficulty data, so you are writing on instinct
SERP scraping and competitor outline analysis
Rank tracking and indexing dashboards to tell you if any of it worked
One-click publishing integrations to WordPress, Webflow, Shopify
Someone else's tuned prompts and page templates, which is more of the product than they admit
moatNotes: Mostly rented data rather than owned data: the keyword and SERP numbers come from upstream vendors, and you can rent them too, just less cheaply per query.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the writing was never the bottleneck, the deciding was. People pay to be told which 400 pages to make, to have them published on a schedule without touching a CMS, and to see a chart that suggests the whole exercise is working. A local script that generates unlimited articles about topics nobody searches for is a very efficient way to produce nothing.
notes: The content generator is a weekend; the keyword and SERP data underneath it is a subscription you will end up paying either way.
prompt:
Build a local SEO content factory as a Node 20 CLI. No web UI, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud.

Stack: TypeScript, Node 20, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Anthropic or OpenAI SDK, Zod for config validation, Commander for the CLI. Output is markdown files with YAML frontmatter, shaped for an Astro content collection.

Project layout:
- src/cli.ts, commands: init, plan, generate, link, publish, status
- src/db.ts, SQLite schema for keywords, pages, generations, internal_links
- src/llm.ts, single provider adapter, model and key from .env
- src/templates/, one handlebars template per page type
- content/ output directory of generated markdown
- site.config.yaml, brand voice, product description, target audience, allowed claims, banned words

Commands:
1. init: scaffold site.config.yaml and the SQLite db.
2. plan: read a keywords.csv (columns: keyword, intent, page_type, optional volume), validate with Zod, insert into db, dedupe, flag near-duplicate keywords by trigram similarity.
3. generate: for each pending keyword, build an outline call then a draft call, enforce word count and heading structure, write markdown with frontmatter (title, description, slug, canonical, keyword, updated). Cache raw LLM responses in the db so reruns are cheap. Support --limit and --dry-run.
4. link: build an internal link graph across generated pages, insert 3-6 contextual links per page by keyword match, never orphan a page, never link a page to itself.
5. publish: copy content/ into a target repo path from .env and print a git command. Do not implement CMS APIs.
6. status: table of keyword count, generated, linked, word totals, estimated token spend.

Explicitly out of scope: keyword volume lookups, SERP scraping, rank tracking, backlink data. Add a stub src/providers/keywords.ts with a documented interface so a paid data API can be dropped in later.

Secrets in .env only. Include a README with a 5 minute quickstart and a sample keywords.csv of 10 rows. Add vitest tests for slug generation, dedupe and the internal link builder.
